source: A solid keeps its own shape. A liquid takes the shape of its container but keeps its amount. A gas spreads out to fill any container.
Thinking a powder like sugar or sand is a liquid because it pours. Each grain is a tiny solid that keeps its shape.
Ice, water and steam are all the same stuff: water. They are three states of matter.
A solid keeps its shape. A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container. A gas spreads out to fill the whole space it is in.
Tap a card, then the state it belongs in.
You can pour sand from a bucket. Is sand a liquid?
Sand is a solid, made of many tiny solid grains.
Look at one grain with a hand lens.
Each grain keeps its own shape, and it does not flow on its own when you tip it a little.
Thinking anything that pours is a liquid. Sugar, salt and sand pour because they are many small solid pieces.
Going further. In Gas in a Box you can watch gas particles bounce around and push on the walls.
